description: Since we are focusing on big ideas and cool game designs, we are looking for teammates to help us bring it to life! We welcome anyone who loves space, and we would especially love to find 1 or 2 people who enjoy coding or building simple games (like in Scratch, Roblox, or Python) to join our crew. Let’s create something amazing together!
summary: Cosmic Besties is an interactive, Duolingo-style space academy built specifically for middle schoolers (ages 13–14) that brings NASA’s retired and deep-space missions to life. Since the 1960s, NASA has sent extraordinary rovers, landers, and probes across the Moon, Mars, and the outer solar system, yet most school websites present their history as dry textbook notes. As a 13-year-old who loves space, I designed this app so 20 iconic spacecraft across four sectors (Early Pioneers, Red Planet Mars, Outer Giants & Ice Worlds, and Comet Chasers & Cosmic Hunters) speak in the first person to share where they are, what they discovered, and how they sent their final signals. Players explore 6-branch Interactive Mission Mind Maps to earn Space Coins, play an adaptive Arcade with a smart hint system that gives helpful clues instead of discouraging wrong answers, sketch their own astronaut avatar in the HTML5 Canvas Cadet Art Studio (saved seamlessly in browser localStorage with zero login barriers), and unbox collectible Mystery Capsules. Every mission also features a direct "Explore on Official NASA.gov" button alongside a dedicated Resources Corner powered by real NASA Science (science.nasa.gov), NASA Image Library (images.nasa.gov), and NSSDCA (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov) archives, all built and published as a live web app using Google AI Studio.
details:
Cosmic Besties is an interactive, Duolingo-style space academy built specifically for middle school students that brings NASA’s retired and deep-space missions to life. Instead of reading passive textbook articles, students explore 20 iconic NASA missions grouped into four cosmic sectors (Early Pioneers, Red Planet Mars, Outer Giants & Ice Worlds, and Comet Chasers & Cosmic Hunters). Every spacecraft speaks in a warm, first-person voice to share where it is, what it discovered, and what happened to its final signal. Clicking any mission opens a 6-branch Interactive Mission Mind Map (Origin & Engineering, Cosmic Journey, Deep Discoveries, Survival & Drama, Final Signal & Fate, and Mission Legacy) that rewards curiosity with Space Coins. Students can then test their knowledge in an adaptive Arcade (featuring an infinite trivia quiz, a signal memory-match game, and a launch-order sorting game), draw their own astronaut avatar in the Cadet Art Studio, and spend their earned coins on collectible Mystery Capsules. Every mission also includes a direct "Explore on Official NASA.gov" button alongside a dedicated Resources Corner linking straight to NASA’s official archives.

Benefits & Intended Impact Most space education websites present historic spacecraft as dry lists of dates and technical specs, which quickly loses the attention of middle schoolers. By combining emotional storytelling, game-based rewards, and zero-login instant access, Forgotten Giants of Space makes real space history feel personal, exciting, and approachable. My goal is to help students my age connect emotionally with NASA's robotic explorers, build curiosity about STEM and planetary science, and learn how to verify space facts using real NASA public archives.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered: As a teen building for teens, I focused heavily on what actually keeps kids engaged without feeling like homework:

  • First-Person Storytelling & Hint-Based Learning: Giving spacecraft their own voices makes them feel like real heroes, while the Arcade's smart hint system gives players a helpful 1-sentence character clue and a second chance instead of discouraging them when they miss a question.
  • Creative Self-Expression & Collection: Adding an interactive drawing pad for custom avatars and Mystery Capsule card packs gives students creative ownership and a fun reason to keep exploring all 20 missions.
  • Privacy & Frictionless Access: Because the app is designed for students, I avoided logins, passwords, or personal data collection by saving all progress, Space Coins, and custom drawings locally in the browser.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Development & Live Hosting: Built and deployed as a public web app using Google AI Studio (Build Mode).
  • Frontend & Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, TypeScript / JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas API (for the Cadet Art Studio drawing pad), and Browser localStorage (for instant, no-login progress and coin saving).
  • NASA Open Data & Archives: NASA Science Missions (science.nasa.gov), NASA Image & Video Library API (images-api.nasa.gov), NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov), and the NASA Open Data Portal (data.nasa.gov).
